canonical_statement: The guideline updates KDIGO guidance for the prevention, diagnosis, evaluation, and treatment of hepatitis C virus infection in people with chronic kidney disease, including patients receiving dialysis and kidney transplant candidates and recipients.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: The 2022 update revised Chapters 2, 4, and 5, while Chapters 1 and 3 were carried forward unchanged from the 2018 guideline because KDIGO judged them current.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: The evidence review formulated questions using PICOS criteria, used predefined eligibility criteria and extraction forms, and separated evidence review responsibilities from the Work Group role in writing and grading recommendations.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: Updated searches used MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, with final electronic searches on February 1, 2022 and additional focused conference-abstract searches and studies known to the Work Group through April 2022.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: KDIGO graded evidence and recommendation strength using GRADE, with Level 1 or Level 2 recommendations paired with evidence grades A through D; ungraded statements were reserved for general guidance such as testing, referral, and routine care.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: The draft guideline underwent public review in February 2022 and was revised based on external review feedback before final approval.

canonical_statement: KDIGO states that its literature searches were intended to be comprehensive but were not exhaustive: specialty and regional databases were not searched, journals were not hand-searched, review articles and textbook chapters were not systematically searched, and conference screening was limited by meeting and recency.

canonical_statement: We recommend screening all patients for HCV infection at the time of initial evaluation of CKD.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend using an immunoassay followed by nucleic acid testing (NAT) if immunoassay is positive.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend screening all patients for HCV infection upon initiation of in-center hemodialysis or upon transfer from another dialysis facility or modality.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend using NAT alone or an immunoassay followed by NAT if immunoassay is positive.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We suggest screening all patients for HCV infection upon initiation of peritoneal dialysis or home hemodialysis.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend screening all patients for HCV infection at the time of evaluation for kidney transplantation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend screening for HCV infection with immunoassay or NAT in in-center hemodialysis patients every 6 months.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: Report any new HCV infection identified in a hemodialysis patient to the appropriate public health authority.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: In units with a new HCV infection, we recommend that all patients be tested for HCV infection and that the frequency of subsequent HCV testing be increased.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend that hemodialysis patients with resolved HCV infection undergo repeat testing every 6 months using NAT to detect possible re-infection.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We suggest that patients have serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) level checked upon initiation of in-center hemodialysis or upon transfer from another facility.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We suggest that hemodialysis patients have ALT level checked monthly.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend assessing HCV-infected patients with CKD for liver fibrosis.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend an initial noninvasive evaluation of liver fibrosis.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: When the cause of liver disease is uncertain or noninvasive testing results are discordant, consider liver biopsy.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend assessment for portal hypertension in CKD patients with suspected advanced fibrosis (F3-F4).

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend assessing all patients for kidney disease at the time of HCV infection diagnosis.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: Screen for kidney disease with urinalysis and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR).

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: If there is no evidence of kidney disease at initial evaluation, patients who remain NAT-positive should undergo repeat screening for kidney disease.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend that all CKD patients with a history of HCV infection, whether NAT-positive or not, be followed up regularly to assess for progression of kidney disease.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend that all CKD patients with a history of HCV infection, whether NAT-positive or not, be screened and, if appropriate, vaccinated against hepatitis A virus (HAV) and hepatitis B virus (HBV), and screened for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend that all patients with CKD (G1-G5), on dialysis (G5D), and kidney transplant recipients (G1T-G5T) with HCV be evaluated for direct-acting antiviral (DAA)-based therapy as outlined in Figure 1.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend that the choice of specific regimen be based on prior treatment history, drug-drug interactions, GFR, stage of hepatic fibrosis, kidney and liver transplant candidacy, and comorbidities. If pangenotypic regimens are not available, HCV genotype (and subtype) should guide the choice of treatment (Figure 1).

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: Treat kidney transplant candidates in collaboration with the transplant center to optimize timing of therapy.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend pre-treatment assessment for drug-drug interactions between the DAA-based regimen and other concomitant medications including immunosuppressive drugs in kidney transplant recipients.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend that calcineurin inhibitor levels be monitored during and after DAA treatment in kidney transplant recipients.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: All patients with CKD (G1-G5), on dialysis (G5D), and kidney transplant recipients (G1T-G5T) with HCV should undergo testing for hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection prior to DAA therapy.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: If hepatitis B surface antigen [HBsAg] is present, the patient should undergo assessment for HBV therapy.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: If HBsAg is absent but markers of prior HBV infection (HBcAb-positive with or without HBsAb) are detected, exclude HBV reactivation with HBV DNA testing if levels of liver function tests rise during DAA therapy.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend that hemodialysis facilities adhere to standard infection control procedures including hygienic precautions that effectively prevent transfer of blood and blood-contaminated ﬂuids between patients to prevent transmission of blood-borne pathogens (see Table 1).

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend regular observational audits of infection control procedures in hemodialysis units.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend not using dedicated dialysis machines for HCV-infected patients.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We suggest not isolating HCV-infected hemodialysis patients.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We suggest that the dialyzers of HCV-infected patients can be reused if there is adherence to standard infection control procedures.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend that hemodialysis centers examine and track all HCV test results to identify new cases of HCV infections in their patients.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend that aggressive measures be taken to improve hand hygiene (and proper glove use), injection safety, and environmental cleaning and disinfection when a new case of HCV is identified that is likely to be dialysis-related.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: Strategies to prevent HCV transmission within hemodialysis units should prioritize adherence to standard infection control practices and should not primarily rely upon the treatment of HCV-infected patients.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend kidney transplantation as the best therapeutic option for patients with CKD G5 irrespective of presence of HCV infection.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We suggest that all kidney transplant candidates with HCV be evaluated for severity of liver disease and presence of portal hypertension prior to acceptance for kidney transplantation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend that patients with HCV, compensated cirrhosis, and no portal hypertension undergo isolated kidney transplantation and that patients with decompensated cirrhosis or clinically significant portal hypertension (i.e., hepatic venous pressure gradient ≥10 mm Hg or evidence of portal hypertension on imaging or exam) undergo a simultaneous liver-kidney transplantation. Treatment of those with mild-to-moderate portal hypertension should be determined on a case-by-case basis.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend referring patients with HCV and decompensated cirrhosis for combined liver-kidney transplantation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: Timing of HCV treatment in relation to kidney transplantation (before vs. after) should be based on donor type (living vs. deceased donor), wait-list times by donor type, center-specific policies governing the use of kidneys from HCV-infected deceased donors, and severity of liver fibrosis.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend that all kidney transplant candidates with HCV be considered for DAA therapy, either before or after transplantation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We suggest that HCV-infected kidney transplant candidates with a living kidney donor be considered for treatment before or shortly after transplantation depending on the anticipated timing of transplantation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend that all kidney donors be screened for HCV infection with both immunoassay and NAT (if NAT is available).

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: After assessment of liver fibrosis, HCV-infected potential living kidney donors who do not have cirrhosis should undergo HCV treatment before donation if the recipient is HCV-uninfected; they can be accepted for donation if they achieve sustained virologic response (SVR) and remain otherwise eligible to be a donor.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend that kidneys from HCV-infected donors be considered regardless of HCV status of potential kidney transplant recipients.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: When transplanting kidneys from HCV-infected donors into HCV-uninfected recipients, transplant centers must ensure that patients receive education and are engaged in discussion with sufficient information to provide informed consent. Patients should be informed of the risks and benefits of transplantation with an HCV-infected kidney, including the need for DAA treatment.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: When transplanting kidneys from HCV-infected donors into HCV-uninfected recipients, transplant centers should confirm availability of DAAs for initiation in the early post-transplant period.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend that kidney transplant recipients being treated with DAAs be evaluated for the need for dose adjustments of concomitant immunosuppressants.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We suggest that patients previously infected with HCV who achieved SVR before transplantation undergo testing by NAT 3 months after transplantation or if liver dysfunction occurs.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: Kidney transplant recipients with cirrhosis should have the same liver disease follow-up as non-transplant patients, as outlined in the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) guidelines.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: HCV-infected kidney transplant recipients should be tested at least every 6 months for proteinuria.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We suggest that patients who develop new-onset proteinuria (either urine protein-creatinine ratio > 1 g/g or 24-hour urine protein > 1 g on 2 or more occasions) have an allograft biopsy with immunofluorescence and electron microscopy included in the analysis.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend treatment with a DAA regimen in patients with post-transplant HCV-associated glomerulonephritis.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: HCV-infected patients with a typical presentation of immune-complex proliferative glomerulonephritis can be managed without a confirmatory kidney biopsy. However, a biopsy may be indicated in certain clinical circumstances (Figure 4).

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend that patients with HCV-associated glomerulonephritis receive antiviral therapy.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend that patients with HCV-associated glomerulonephritis, stable kidney function, and without nephrotic syndrome be treated with DAAs prior to other treatments.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend that patients with cryoglobulinemic flare or rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis be treated with both DAAs and immunosuppressive agents with or without plasma exchange.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: The decision whether to use immunosuppressive agents in patients with nephrotic syndrome should be individualized.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend immunosuppressive therapy in patients with histologically active HCV-associated glomerulonephritis who do not respond to antiviral therapy, particularly those with cryoglobulinemic kidney disease.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: We recommend rituximab as the ﬁrst-line immunosuppressive treatment.
